notes: Wayfair UK (wayfair.co.uk) has a genuine, independently-run Pets department at /pets/, distinct from Wayfair US, AllModern, Birch Lane and Joss & Main (per the assignment note, the three siblings have NO pet category at all; Wayfair US does; wayfair.co.uk was independently re-derived here and also has a real one). ACCESS: robots.txt (200, no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web disallow) allows /*/sb0/, /*/sb1/, /*/sb2/ and lists sitemap indexes. Plain fetch of the homepage hit a PerimeterX px-captcha 429, but curl_cffi with impersonate='chrome124' cleared every /cat/ and /sb0/ page fetched after that (used for all ~35 pages retrieved), consistent with the prior Home-Decor pass's note for this same host. DISCOVERY: found /pets/cat/pets-c477714.html (the 'Pets' landing hub) via https://www.wayfair.co.uk/seo-category-sitemap~0.xml (grep for 'pet'), then built the tree by (1) reading the pets-hub page's own embedded nav block for its direct sb0/cat children, then (2) fetching each species/type sub-hub (Dog, Cat, Bird & Small Pet, Chicken, Dog Beds, Dog Kennels/Crates/Cages & Pet Carriers, Dog Bowls & Feeding Supplies, Cat Trees/Perches/Scratchers, Litter Boxes, Pet Gates/Fences/Doors) and diffing its links against the pets-hub baseline to isolate that hub's own further children, same method as the archived Lighting/Home-Decor pass for this host. QTY: read from the page's own RSC/Next.js payload embedded in the HTML (escaped two ways on this rendering path -- backslash-quoted \"resultCount\":N on some pages, HTML-entity "resultCount":N on others); cross-checked resultCount against numberOfItems on every page where both were present -- always agreed. 'totalCount' fields were present but discarded (unrelated widget counts, same trap noted in the archived pass). GROUPING DECISIONS: /pets/cat/ hub pages that have real further sb0/cat children were emitted as is_group rows (qty null) even though several of them also carry their own resultCount (e.g. 'Dog' hub=3774, 'Dog Beds & Raised Dog Beds'=1496) -- that hub-level count is the parent aggregate of its children and was not used as a leaf qty, to avoid double-counting, matching the precedent set in this company's archived Lighting pass (e.g. 'Ceiling Lights' recorded qty=null there for the same reason). EXACT DUPLICATE MERGED: /pets/sb0/all-cat-trees-perches-scratchers-c1877060.html reported resultCount=1687, identical to its parent hub /pets/cat/cat-trees-perches-scratchers-c1876370.html (also 1687) -- same underlying listing reached two ways; only the hub grouping row was kept, the 'All Cat Trees...' sb0 duplicate was dropped per the same-count/same-listing merge rule. KEPT AS DISTINCT (not merged) despite overlap: 'All Dog Beds' (1358) alongside Small/Medium/Large/Extra Large Dog Beds (520/674/483/254) -- these are NOT identical counts to each other or to the parent (sum of the four sizes, 1931, exceeds All Dog Beds' own 1358, proving cross-listing rather than a clean partition) so each is a genuinely different PLP and all were kept per the brief's 'genuinely different PLPs -> keep both' rule, flagged here only as a transparency note, not as an exclusion. Similarly kept 'All Bird Cages' (283) alongside its narrower style siblings Large Floor/Play Top/Table Top Bird Cages (126/15/31) for the same reason. ABSENCE CHECK: scanned the Dog hub page's full payload for toy/collar/leash/harness/coat/clothing/training/walk keywords -- all hits were unrelated (kids' ride-on toys, furniture coat racks) or zero; Wayfair UK's Pets department carries no dog/cat toys, collars, leashes, harnesses, clothing or training-aid categories at all (confirmed absent, not merely unfound -- verified via full nav-payload keyword scan, not just site search). EXCLUDED as marketing/nav pages (never a category): every '-sale-' variant found alongside a real category (Cat Furniture Sale, Dog Furniture Sale, Pet Furniture Sale, Cat Trees Perches & Scratchers Sale, Dog Beds Sale, Dog Bowls & Feeding Supplies Sale, Dog Crates & Carriers Sale, Litter Boxes Sale, Pet Gates Fences & Doors Sale, Chicken Sale). No pet-food/consumable or medical/veterinary categories were found anywhere in the tree, so no MANUAL REVIEW flags were needed for those two open policy gaps. Zero-product categories: none observed (every leaf above had qty>0); none dropped for that reason.
